- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility or sentiment swings, dampen forecast magnitude.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is low and price is near support, model often fails to recognize reversal; add a small upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to avoid undershooting.
- If sentiment is high but price is near resistance, model may overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false breakout.
